amazon_bundle_check: I ran four Amazon searches with amzcheck (2026-11-15): 'EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus 220W bifacial solar panel', 'EF ECOFLOW DELTA 3 Plus with 220W solar panel', 'DELTA 3 Plus 220W Bifacial Solar Panel solar generator' and 'ecoflow delta 3 plus solar panel bundle'. wins.need: Start with one panel and add more later
wins.claim: The unit has two separate 500 W solar inputs (1,000 W total). By arithmetic, it can take four of the bundle's panels, two in series on each input: 2 × 21.5 V Voc = 43.0 V (limit 60 V), 11.9 A (limit 15 A), 2 × 18.4 V × 11.9 A = 438 W (limit 500 W). That gives 876 W of front-side panel rating. The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 tops out at 600 W of solar input.
wins.figure: 1,000 W solar input (2 × 500 W, 11–60 V, 15 A) vs Anker C1000 Gen 2 at 600 W. Room for 4 × 220 W panels = 876 W (arithmetic)
wins.who: EcoFlow manual and EcoFlow panel spec page; Anker product page; arithmetic labelled

wins.need: Keeping a router, NAS or PC running through a blackout
wins.claim: StorageReview measured how fast it switches to battery: faster than EcoFlow's own 10 ms spec. BLUETTI (Elite 100 V2) and Jackery (HomePower 1000 v2) only publish claims of 10 ms or under. These are claims, not measurements from the same test.
wins.figure: just over 8 ms measured (EcoFlow spec <10 ms)

wins.need: Fast refill from the wall before a storm
wins.claim: The Solar Lab measured a full AC recharge in 55 minutes. OutdoorGearLab measured AC charge rate on the DELTA 3, the non-Plus sibling with the same 1,024 Wh battery, at 1,229 Wh/hr. In the same OutdoorGearLab test, the Anker C1000 Gen 2 charged at 1,097 Wh/hr and the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 at 563 Wh/hr.
wins.figure: 55 min 0–100% (The Solar Lab); sibling DELTA 3 1,229 Wh/hr vs Anker 1,097 and Jackery 563 Wh/hr (OutdoorGearLab)
wins.who: The Solar Lab; OutdoorGearLab (RJ Spurrier, Kenji Mowrey, Sentry Kelly)

wins.need: Home backup with a gas generator that starts itself
wins.claim: EcoFlow says the automatic start-stop on its Smart Generator 3000 (Dual Fuel) works only with the DELTA 3, DELTA 3 Plus and DELTA 3 Ultra Plus. The generator is not sold in California.
wins.figure: Auto start-stop: DELTA 3 / DELTA 3 Plus / DELTA 3 Ultra Plus only

wins.claim: StorageReview measured low fan noise under a mid-size load.
wins.figure: about 30 dB at 600 W; about 40 dB maximum at higher loads

wins.need: Charging from the vehicle in an RV or van
wins.claim: With EcoFlow's optional 800 W Alternator Charger, StorageReview lists a full charge in 1.3 hours.

weak.claim: The bundled panel fills less than half of one solar input. Even at full rated output, a refill takes hours, not the 70 minutes EcoFlow advertises for 1,000 W of panels.
weak.figure: 220 W front rating vs 1,000 W input. Best case 1,024 Wh ÷ 220 W ≈ 4.7 h with no losses (arithmetic); real sun is slower

weak.claim: Runs hot under heavy load, and The Solar Lab saw the fans cycle erratically
weak.figure: 138°F internal on the first 1,573 W run; second run 32 min at 82% efficiency, ending at 126°F

weak.claim: Measured surge fell short of the claim
weak.figure: about 2,600 W held for about a minute, then shutdown (3,600 W claimed)

weak.claim: Heavier than the main 1 kWh rivals
weak.figure: 27.6 lb (StorageReview spec table) vs Anker C1000 Gen 2 at 24.9 lb and BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 at 25 lb (maker pages). The panel adds 15.4 lb, so the kit is about 43 lb (arithmetic)

weak.claim: Lower continuous AC output than the Anker
weak.figure: 1,800 W vs Anker C1000 Gen 2 at 2,000 W

weak.claim: The panel's warranty is much shorter than the power station's
weak.figure: 12 months on the panel (US) vs 5 years on the DELTA 3 Plus
The Solar Lab lists 'No built-in light' as a con

weak.claim: Measured usable energy is level with rivals, not ahead
weak.figure: 910 Wh of 1,024 Wh (StorageReview). OutdoorGearLab measured Jackery 1000 v2 910 Wh, Anker C1000 Gen 2 890 Wh, BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 890 Wh (different lab, so not a like-for-like test)

wins_for: Buyers who want a 1 kWh kit now and plan to add panels: two 500 W inputs take up to four of the bundle's panels (arithmetic from maker limits)
A home office or network closet that needs a fast switch to battery: 8 ms measured by StorageReview
Outage plans built around EcoFlow's Smart Generator 3000, since only DELTA 3-family units get its auto start-stop
RV and van owners who will add the 800 W alternator charger (1.3 h full charge, StorageReview)
People who later want more than 1 kWh: EcoFlow lists 1–5 kWh with an extra battery
not_for: The cheapest 1 kWh panel kit: today the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 + 200W costs $729 at BLUETTI and the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 + 200W costs $779.99 on Amazon. The EcoFlow bundle price could not be read today
Carrying the kit far, such as walk-in camping: the Anker C1000 Gen 2 (24.9 lb) or BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (25 lb) is lighter
Running loads near 1,800 W for a long time or starting loads that surge above 2,600 W: The Solar Lab measured heat and a surge shutdown. The Anker C1000 Gen 2 is rated 2,000 W continuous
Whole-house backup: 1 kWh with one extra battery is the wrong class. Look at whole-home systems such as EcoFlow's TITAN line
Fast solar refill with only the bundled panel: one 220 W panel needs about 4.7 h even in ideal sun

rivals.where_it_beats_ours: Lower kit price than EcoFlow's last-seen $919 (that figure is from 2026-11-08 and not confirmed today). Lighter at 25 lb vs 27.6 lb. Also 1,000 W solar input (maker page)

record.name: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus Solar Generator (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W) with NextGen 220 W Bifacial Solar Panel
specs: 2 × 500 W MPPT (1,000 W total), each 11–60 V, 15 A
220 W front / 175 W rear bifacial, N-type TOPCon, 25.00% efficiency, IP68
Voc 21.5 V (Vmp 18.4 V), Isc 12.4 A front; approx. 15.4 lb
record.warranty: 5 years on the DELTA 3 Plus (https://www.ecoflow.com/us/delta-3-series-portable-power-station); 12 months on the NextGen 220 W panel in the US (https://www.ecoflow.com/us/new-220w-bifacial-solar-panel)
record.summary: A 1 kWh EcoFlow power station with two 500 W solar inputs, sold with one 220 W bifacial panel. The panel uses less than half of one input, so the kit is built for adding panels later. StorageReview measured 910 Wh usable and an 8 ms switch to battery.
record.fit: Home-office and short-outage backup, EcoFlow Smart Generator owners, and RV owners who will add panels or the 800 W alternator charger.
caveats: One 220 W panel needs at least about 4.7 h of ideal sun for a full refill (arithmetic from EcoFlow specs)
The Solar Lab measured 138°F internal at 1,573 W and a surge shutdown at about 2,600 W vs the 3,600 W claim
27.6 lb unit plus a 15.4 lb panel; heavier than the Anker C1000 Gen 2 (24.9 lb) and BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (25 lb)
The panel's warranty is 12 months vs 5 years on the power station
No EcoFlow listing for this bundle on Amazon US as of 2026-11-15
